Page of 27-01-2026 confirms: plan of 14 January to extend to 23.00 in all sectors reconsidered; from 1 May 2026 only sectors B and F (Mon-Sat 09-23); reason: Rotterdam-West already runs to 23.00 and drivers would move to Schiedam-Oost and Nieuw-Mathenesse; A, C, D, E unchanged. Error: the page says the municipality will monitor the effect on traffic in sectors B and F, and on that basis may decide LATER whether paid parking is relevant for A, C, D and E (hours there stay the same 'voorlopig'). The draft says it would monitor the effect on those sectors (A, C, D, E). The page was written before 1 May, so the extension is an announcement.
items.corrected_text: On 27 January 2026 the municipality announced that it had reconsidered its plan of 14 January to extend paid parking to 23.00 in all sectors: from 1 May 2026 the extension would apply only to sector B (Schiedam-Oost) and sector F (Nieuw-Mathenesse), Monday to Saturday, so that drivers from Rotterdam-West, where paid parking already runs to 23.00, do not move to Schiedam-Oost and Nieuw-Mathenesse. Sectors A, C, D and E keep their current hours for the time being. The municipality said it would watch the effect on traffic pressure in sectors B and F and could later decide, on that basis, whether paid parking is relevant for sectors A, C, D and E.

items.corrected_text: The municipality's page (undated; read 21 October 2026) says paid parking has applied in Nieuw-Mathenesse (sector F) since Friday 1 May 2026, Monday to Saturday 09.00-23.00 at 2.39 euros an hour, to support a car-light Glasbuurt with about 1,300 new homes whose future residents are to park in two future garages and pay for a space there to make the garages financially feasible. There was no support survey because the area is a business park with no residents; businesses can get permits based on their number of staff, and residents of other neighbourhoods cannot get sector F permits.

corrected_summary: Schiedam, next to Rotterdam, runs paid on-street parking in the historic centre and the surrounding neighbourhoods, split into sectors A to F. Under the 2026 tariff table (council decision of 11 November 2025) sector A, the centre, costs 3.32 euros an hour and the other sectors 2.39 euros, resident permits start at 90.10 euros a year, and a post-assessment costs 82 euros. A municipal annex that took effect on 1 May 2026 extended paid hours to 23.00 in sector B (Schiedam-Oost) and the new sector F (Nieuw-Mathenesse) only, announced as a way to stop spill-over from Rotterdam-West; sector F supports the planned Glasbuurt with about 1,300 homes and two garages that are still to be built. Further neighbourhoods can only get regulated parking after a formal support survey that needs requests from 10 percent of adult residents in a neighbourhood; the interim count of 20 April 2026 was far below that everywhere. Second resident permits in Schiedam-Oost (sector B) are capped at 250 addresses with a waiting list. The centre garages are ABC (Interparking, 325 spaces) and the Passage garage (280 spaces), both with the first hour free, plus the Stadserf garage, whose only tariff data (an old open-data registry record) is outdated; the municipality also lists the P+R Schiedam Centrum garage (more than 750 spaces, with a link to ParkingYou for tariffs), P+R Horvathweg (64 spaces, Q-Park) and free parking at Vijfsluizen metro station. New developments are mostly policy-led: mobility norms from July 2024 set a parking norm of zero for most inner-city projects. On charging, the municipality reports more than 700 public charge points, no longer accepts resident requests for new ones from 1 January 2026, and plans forecast-based expansion with new operators from 2027. A newspaper report on a coalition aim of regulated parking south of the A20 could not be verified. No utilisation statements from the municipality or operators were found.
